description:
Remove the test hook from the product binary and the runner configuration, now that profiled fixtures build cheaply on first use.

## Background

`crates/jit/src/main.rs:1787-1793` compiles a hidden `__test-fixture-setup` subcommand under `cfg(feature = "test-support")`, which the crate's self dev-dependency (`crates/jit/Cargo.toml:106`) enables for every test build of the binary. `.config/nextest.toml` runs it as the `default-repository-fixture` and `dogfood-repository-fixture` setup scripts, each filtered by module prefixes and individual test names. Consumers read a run-bound receipt (`prepare_nextest_profiled_repository_fixture`, `nextest_profiled_repository_fixture` and the receipt tests in `crates/jit/src/test_utils.rs`), and `PROFILED_REPOSITORY_FIXTURE_ENV_LOCK` serialises receipt-environment access beside `EnvGuard`. `fast_docs_templates/template_apply_tests.rs` and `scratch_build/build_profile_policy_tests.rs` parse the nextest configuration.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The `jit` binary has no `__test-fixture-setup` subcommand in any build configuration.
- [hard] REQ-02: `.config/nextest.toml` declares no profiled-repository setup script, and no profiled-repository script filter that names individual tests or test modules remains.
- [hard] REQ-03: Profiled-fixture consumers obtain their repository from the input-keyed cache on first use. The receipt code, its environment variables, its tests and `PROFILED_REPOSITORY_FIXTURE_ENV_LOCK` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-04: Tests that parsed the removed setup scripts assert what remains of the runner configuration, or no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-05: `dev/TESTING.md` describes profiled fixtures as built in the suite on first use.
title: Fixture setup runs inside the suite with no runner hook
